preamble: Fronting and unrounding of the close back rounded [u] to the near-close near-front [ɪ]. In Southern Yiddish (Poylish and Galitsyaner), the short u of Northern (Litvish) and Standard Yiddish corresponds to a front unrounded vowel: Middle High German sunne 'sun' gives Poylish זון /zɪn/ against Litvish and YIVO /zʊn/, and hunt 'dog' gives /hɪnt/ against /hʊnt/. Short /ɪ/ of Yiddish is typically a near-close [ɪ].

examples.note: Northern (Litvish) and YIVO Yiddish keep the inherited vowel as /zʊn/; Southern Yiddish fronted and unrounded short u.
